chosen_reason: Factory-built Boeing 767-316F(ER)(WL) (not a BCF conversion), LATAM Cargo Colombia, wearing the current LATAM CARGO scheme with no special titles. Five free-licence photos spanning 2021-2026 cover both sides, the underside and the tail. The factory freighter matches the ACAP's own 767-300 Freighter drawings exactly (no cabin windows at all, single forward LH passenger door), which is what the -300F pages of D6-58328 document; the twelve BCF conversions in the fleet keep a full row of plugged-and-painted cabin windows and a deactivated door 3.

aircraft.engines: 2x GE CF6-80C2 (same as the -300ER passenger fleet)
aircraft.winglets: Aviation Partners blended winglets - confirmed on the 2026-06-20 photographs
aircraft.factory_or_conversion: FACTORY FREIGHTER. Clean skin with no cabin windows and no plugged-window outlines anywhere; only the forward LH passenger door. Cross-checked against CC-CXE and N568LA, which are BCF conversions and show the whole plugged window row plus an 'EXIT INOPERATIVE' door 3.
aircraft.sources_note: MSN / line number / dates come from PlaneLogger (planespotters, airfleets, rzjets, ATDB and FR24 all returned HTTP 403 from this environment), so they rest on a single database and are flagged as unverified against a second source. Everything used for the model itself is measured on the photographs below or read from the Boeing ACAP.

livery: LATAM CARGO, the group's unified cargo scheme (the last LAN-Cargo-liveried 767F, N418LA, was repainted at Etihad Engineering and announced 2025-10-06). White fuselage; the passenger fleet's fin sash unchanged; a rear indigo wedge that is smaller than the passenger one; a two-line LATAM/CARGO lockup with the symbol forward; white registration inside the wedge; national flag and country name behind the windshield. NOT the old LAN Cargo or ABSA scheme, and NOT the passenger application.

photos.author: Duncan Kirk
photos.view: near-pure port side profile, taxiing, sunlit, clean sky
photos.notes: PRIMARY measurement photo. Every livery number in spec_763f.json -> livery_n536la was measured here: the rear wedge boundaries, the registration inside the indigo, the two-line lockup, the type title. Same photographer and airport as the 767-300ER's CC-CWY reference. Being a BCF it also documents the plugged window row and the deactivated door 3, which is exactly what N536LA does NOT have.

photos.author: Sg1959
photos.view: port side, on approach with gear down, clean sky
photos.notes: The target registration in its current state. Confirms: no cabin windows, winglets, 'BOEING767-300F' type title, white N536LA inside the indigo wedge, COLOMBIA flag behind the windshield.

photos.author: Colin Cooke Photo
photos.notes: Starboard reference: the R1 service door, the absence of a main deck cargo door on this side, and the mirrored lockup (symbol still forward of the wordmark).

photos.author: jounigripen
photos.view: from below on climb-out - the only view of the belly and of both winglet faces
photos.notes: Settles two things no side view can: the belly carries only the LATAM symbol (forward, around x 9-12 m), not the passenger fleet's wordmark at x 24-31; and the winglets are indigo on the outboard face, CORAL on the inboard face.

photos.author: Liam Thompson
photos.view: port side on the ground at LAX, sharpest ground shot in the set
photos.notes: Second factory-freighter reference (clean skin). Also the airframe whose repaint out of LAN Cargo colours was announced 2025-10-06. Its rear type title reads 'BOEING 767-300ER' although it is a factory 767-316F(ER) - verified at 4x, an oddity of the real aircraft.

photos.author: MarcelX42
photos.notes: Documents an INTERIM state, not the target: full LATAM CARGO titles on a plain white fin with no sash and no wedge (ex-MasAir, transferred 2022-09-03). By 2026-01-24 the same aircraft wears the full scheme. Kept as evidence that the scheme has to be dated.

photos.author: kitmasterbloke
photos.notes: Carries the 'AVION SOLIDARIO' special titles, which is why N420LA was not chosen. Both winglet faces are in frame.

photos.author: Colin Cooke Photo
photos.notes: Shows that the fin sash rises aft on the starboard side too - the same artwork in (x,z) on both sides, as on the passenger 767.

photos.author: Colin Cooke Photo
photos.notes: Best plugged-window evidence together with CC-CXE: the whole cabin window row is readable in the paint on a conversion.

photos.author: Liam Thompson
photos.notes: Conversion reference: plugged windows and the 'BOEING 767-300BCF' type title.

photos.author: 4300streetcar
photos.view: main deck cargo door OPEN, being unloaded
photos.notes: CONTROL EXPERIMENT. No free-licence LATAM Cargo photograph resolves the closed main deck cargo door - the paint and the tight seal hide the outline, and the door sits under the LATAM symbol and the first letters of the wordmark. This UPS 767-300F with the door open confirms the ACAP independently: forward, PORT side, immediately aft of the L1 door.

photos.author: Doronenko
photos.notes: Control for the CLOSED door: on a UPS 767-300F the main deck cargo door outline is readable under contrast enhancement, immediately aft of the L1 door.

policy: The photographs themselves are NOT redistributed in this repository (see NOTICE.md and the folder .gitignore). URL, author, licence and date are recorded here so any measurement can be traced and the attribution the licences require can be met.
not_found: No free-licence photograph of a LATAM Cargo 767 that resolves the CLOSED main deck cargo door; none with the door open. The door in the model therefore rests entirely on the ACAP, cross-checked on a UPS airframe.
No free-licence photograph found on Commons for PR-ABD (in current colours), PR-ACO, CC-BDB, N542LA or N564LA.
CC-CZZ's last free photograph is 2022-08-31 and still shows full LAN Cargo colours; its current scheme is unconfirmed.
